title: Teachers appointed
summary: Amulon gains favor with the king of the Lamanites, who grants that Amulon and his brethren should be appointed teachers over his people. The Lamanites had taken possession of Shemlon, Shilom, and Amulon, and the king had appointed kings over those lands. The king is named Laman after his father and rules a numerous people.
locations: Unspecified location; the lands of Shemlon, Shilom, and Amulon are named but are not established as the site of the grant

explicit_facts.text: Amulon gained favor with the king of the Lamanites, who granted that Amulon and his brethren should be appointed teachers over his people, including people in Shemlon, Shilom, and Amulon.
The Lamanites had taken possession of those lands, and the king had appointed kings over them.
The king was named Laman after his father and ruled a numerous people.

unspecified_visual_details: The appearance of the people and places
Where and how the king made the grant

narration.text: the king of the Lamanites granted unto him and his brethren that they should be appointed teachers over his people

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The appointments of kings over the lands are reported as prior events, not shown occurring alongside the grant concerning teachers.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict an unreported meeting, appointment ceremony, or coronation.
Do not invent names or appearances for Amulon's brethren or the kings appointed over the lands.

title: The language taught
summary: He appointed teachers of the brethren of Amulon in every land possessed by his people. The language of Nephi began to be taught among the Lamanites. The people were friendly with one another but did not know God. The brethren of Amulon did not teach them about the Lord, the law of Moses, or Abinadi’s words; they taught them to keep their record and write to one another.
characters: The appointing figure, identified only as “he” in the supplied verses
locations: Lands possessed by his people; specific locations unspecified

explicit_facts.text: He appointed teachers of the brethren of Amulon in every land possessed by his people; the supplied verses do not identify him further.
The language of Nephi began to be taught among all the people of the Lamanites.
The people were friendly with one another but did not know God.
The brethren of Amulon did not teach them about the Lord their God, the law of Moses, or the words of Abinadi.
They taught the people to keep their record and write to one another.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A record could visually suggest the reported teaching about recordkeeping without depicting a particular lesson.
unspecified_visual_details: The teachers’ individual identities and appearances
The specific settings and writing materials

narration.text: But they taught them that they should keep their record, and that they might write one to another.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: These verses report teaching across lands, not one specific lesson.
prohibited_inventions: Do not identify the appointing figure using verses outside the supplied text.
Do not depict a specific lesson about the Lord, the law of Moses, or Abinadi’s words.
Do not invent a particular classroom, occasion, teacher, or exchange of dialogue.

title: Trade and plunder
summary: The Lamanites begin to increase in riches and trade with one another. The account describes their worldly cunning and delight in wickedness and plunder, except among their own brethren.

explicit_facts.text: The Lamanites began to increase in riches and trade with one another.
They became cunning and wise in worldly matters and delighted in wickedness and plunder, except among their own brethren.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Trading can be represented by Lamanites exchanging goods.
unspecified_visual_details: Specific goods, setting, and any particular act of plunder.

narration.text: And thus the Lamanites began to increase in riches, and began to trade one with another and wax great,

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The description of worldly wisdom is narration, not a separate visible event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a specific raid or victim not identified in the text.

title: Amulon exercises authority over Alma and his brethren
summary: Amulon begins to exercise authority over Alma and his brethren, persecutes Alma, causes his children to persecute their children, and puts tasks and task-masters over them.
characters: Children of Alma and his brethren

explicit_facts.text: Amulon began to exercise authority over Alma and his brethren, persecuted Alma, and caused his children to persecute their children.
Amulon knew that Alma had been one of the king’s priests, had believed the words of Abinadi, and had been driven out before the king; Amulon was wroth with Alma.
Amulon was subject to king Laman but exercised authority over Alma and his brethren, putting tasks and task-masters over them.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Task-masters may be shown overseeing Alma and his brethren as they carry out tasks.
unspecified_visual_details: The location, the particular tasks, and the appearances of the people are not specified.

narration.text: and put tasks upon them, and put task-masters over them.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Alma's former priesthood and expulsion are background, not events occurring in this scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Alma's earlier expulsion as happening now.
Do not depict king Laman or Abinadi as physically present on the basis of their mention here.
Do not invent dialogue or specific forms of persecution.

title: Silent prayer under guard
summary: Their afflictions lead them to cry mightily to God. Amulon orders them to stop and places guards over them. Alma and his people then pray without raising their voices.

explicit_facts.text: Their afflictions led them to cry mightily to God.
Amulon commanded them to stop their cries and put guards over them to watch them; anyone found calling upon God was to be put to death.
Alma and his people did not raise their voices to the Lord their God, but poured out their hearts to him; he knew their thoughts.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma and his people remain quiet while guards watch them.
unspecified_visual_details: Their surroundings, clothing, postures, and the guards' arrangement are not described.

narration.text: And Alma and his people did not raise their voices to the Lord their God, but did pour out their hearts to him; and he did know the thoughts of their hearts.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: God's knowledge of their thoughts is stated, but no visible appearance is described.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show God visibly or depict an execution.
Do not portray Amulon as present during their silent prayer.

title: The voice of the Lord promises deliverance
summary: The voice of the Lord comes to people in their afflictions, promising comfort, a covenant, deliverance from bondage, and relief from their burdens.
characters: The Lord, heard as a voice

explicit_facts.text: The voice of the Lord came to the people in their afflictions.
The Lord said he knew of their covenant with him and promised to covenant with his people and deliver them from bondage.
The Lord promised to ease the burdens on their shoulders while they were still in bondage, so they could later be witnesses and know that he visits his people in their afflictions.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The people may be shown listening, with burdens on their shoulders.
unspecified_visual_details: The location and the people's appearance.
Any visible source of the voice.

spoken_dialogue.text: Lift up your heads and be of good comfort, for I know of the covenant which ye have made unto me;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

spoken_dialogue.text: and I will covenant with my people and deliver them out of bondage.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

spoken_dialogue.text: And I will also ease the burdens which are put upon your shoulders,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

spoken_dialogue.text: even while you are in bondage;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The Lord is heard as a voice; no visible appearance is described.
The easing of burdens is a promise in this passage, not a separately narrated event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show a visible divine figure or a visible source for the voice.
Do not depict deliverance or the easing of burdens as already occurring.
Do not identify the people or location beyond what these verses state.

title: Burdens made light
summary: The burdens laid upon Alma and his brethren are made light. The Lord strengthens them to bear their burdens with ease, and they submit cheerfully and patiently to his will.

explicit_facts.text: The burdens laid upon Alma and his brethren were made light.
The Lord strengthened them so they could bear their burdens with ease.
They submitted cheerfully and patiently to the will of the Lord.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Calm, cheerful expressions could convey their patient endurance.
unspecified_visual_details: The nature of the burdens and the setting are not stated.
No visible form of the Lord's strengthening is described.

narration.text: the burdens which were laid upon Alma and his brethren were made light;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The easing of the burdens and the Lord's strengthening are stated, but no visible manifestation is specified.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent physical loads, tasks, or a supernatural visual effect.

title: Promise of deliverance
summary: The Lord speaks again, promising deliverance on the morrow and telling Alma that he will lead the people, with the Lord going with him.

explicit_facts.text: Because of their faith and patience, the voice of the Lord came again, promising deliverance from bondage on the morrow.
The Lord told Alma to go before the people and promised to go with him and deliver them.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma may be shown receiving the voice's message.
unspecified_visual_details: How the Lord's voice is represented; Alma's precise posture or surroundings.

spoken_dialogue.text: Be of good comfort, for on the morrow I will deliver you out of bondage.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

spoken_dialogue.text: Thou shalt go before this people,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

spoken_dialogue.text: and I will go with thee and deliver this people out of bondage.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The Lord is heard as a voice; no visible appearance is given.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the Lord visibly.

title: Gathering in the night
summary: Alma and his people gather their flocks and grain throughout the night.

explicit_facts.text: Alma and his people gathered their flocks and grain at night; they spent the night gathering the flocks.

reasonable_visual_inferences: People gathering flocks and grain at night.
unspecified_visual_details: The kind and number of animals, the type and quantity of grain, the lighting, and the surroundings.

narration.text: even all the night-time were they gathering the flocks together.

prohibited_inventions: Do not show a departure or assign a motive for the gathering.

title: The Lamanites sleep
summary: In the morning, the Lord causes a deep sleep to come upon the Lamanites, and all their task-masters are in a profound sleep.

explicit_facts.text: In the morning, the Lord caused a deep sleep to come upon the Lamanites, and all their task-masters were in a profound sleep.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The Lamanites and their task-masters may be shown asleep in the morning.
unspecified_visual_details: Their exact location and sleeping positions.

narration.text: And in the morning the Lord caused a deep sleep to come upon the Lamanites, yea, and all their task-masters were in a profound sleep.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The account attributes the sleep to the Lord but describes no visible divine manifestation.
prohibited_inventions: Do not add a visible figure causing the sleep.

title: Tents in the valley
summary: Alma and his people depart into the wilderness, travel all day, pitch their tents in a valley, and call the valley Alma because he led their way.

explicit_facts.text: Alma and his people departed into the wilderness.
After traveling all day, they pitched their tents in a valley.
They called the valley Alma because he led their way in the wilderness.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The visible moment can show Alma and his people with tents in the valley after the day's travel.
unspecified_visual_details: The valley's terrain, the number and appearance of the people, and the number and appearance of the tents.

narration.text: and when they had traveled all day they pitched their tents in a valley,
and they called the valley Alma, because he led their way in the wilderness.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The departure and day of travel precede the tent-pitching moment; do not depict them as simultaneous events.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict an unspecified departure point or route.
Do not invent speech for the naming of the valley.

title: Thanks in the valley
summary: In the valley of Alma, they thank God for mercy, eased burdens, and deliverance from bondage. The men, women, and children who can speak lift their voices in praise of God.

explicit_facts.text: In the valley of Alma, they thanked God because he had been merciful, eased their burdens, and delivered them from bondage.
None could deliver them from bondage except the Lord their God.
All their men and women and children who could speak lifted their voices in praise of God.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Men, women, and children who can speak may be shown together in the valley, giving thanks.
unspecified_visual_details: Their clothing, positions, and arrangement in the valley are not specified.

narration.text: And they gave thanks to God

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verses narrate their thanks and praise but do not supply the words they spoke.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent words for their thanks or praise.
Do not depict the earlier deliverance as happening during this scene.

title: Leave the valley
summary: The Lord warns Alma that the Lamanites have awakened and are pursuing, commands the people to leave, and promises to stop the pursuers in the valley. Alma's people depart into the wilderness.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord told Alma to hurry out of the land because the Lamanites had awakened and were pursuing them, and promised to stop the Lamanites in the valley.
Alma's people departed from the valley and journeyed into the wilderness.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The people can be shown departing the valley into the wilderness after hearing the warning.
unspecified_visual_details: The form in which the Lord's warning is received; the pursuers' distance and appearance.

spoken_dialogue.text: Haste thee and get thou and this people out of this land,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

spoken_dialogue.text: for the Lamanites have awakened and do pursue thee;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

spoken_dialogue.text: therefore get thee out of this land,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

spoken_dialogue.text: and I will stop the Lamanites in this valley that they come no further in pursuit of this people.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The Lord is described as speaking; no visible appearance is stated.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the Lamanites being stopped; only the promise is given here.

title: Arrival in Zarahemla
summary: After twelve days in the wilderness, they arrived in the land of Zarahemla, and king Mosiah received them with joy.

explicit_facts.text: They had been in the wilderness twelve days.
They arrived in the land of Zarahemla.
King Mosiah received them with joy.

reasonable_visual_inferences: King Mosiah meets the arriving group.
unspecified_visual_details: The precise place and manner of the reception.

narration.text: And after they had been in the wilderness twelve days they arrived in the land of Zarahemla; and king Mosiah did also receive them with joy.

prohibited_inventions: Do not identify the unnamed group or add dialogue or a ceremonial welcome.
